sbh1.1:1.3: *Manuṣyatva* is the abstract noun *manuṣya* + *-tva*, literally 'human-ness.' Asaṅga defines it here as a compound condition: rebirth among humans (1.4) **and** male body with the male sex-faculty (1.5). Translating *manuṣyatva* as bare 'being human' produces a jarring tautology at 1.5 — the male-faculty clause would read as restricting humanness rather than as a sub-condition of a technical category. *Manuṣyatva* is therefore retained in the running translation. The category is the first of the five *ātmasampat* (endowments-from-self) listed at 1.2 and parallels Abhidharmakośa usage; the Śrāvakabhūmi is a *bhikṣu* manual, and the *bhikṣuṇī* lineage has its own treatment elsewhere in the Yogācāra corpus. *Puruṣendriya* at 1.5 is the male sex-faculty as one of the twenty-two *indriyas*, distinct from *puruṣa* (the social-biological category). See glossary entry *manuṣyatva*.
sbh1.1:1.7: *Ārya-āyatana* here means 'noble *locus*' in a **geographical** sense — paralleling *madhya-janapada* (Middle Country) in 1.8, the heartland where dharma transmission concentrates, contrasted with *pratyanta-janapada* (peripheral countries) where renunciant communities and teachings are sparse. The same word *āyatana* recurs at 1.13 (*āyatana-gata prasāda*) with a **doctrinal** referent — the dharma-vinaya as the proper locus of faith — so its two appearances in the *ātmasampat* list do not refer to the same thing. Both are rendered to keep the sense distinct: 'region' for the geographical *āyatana* here, 'sphere' for the doctrinal *āyatana* at 1.13. See glossary entry *āyatana*.
sbh1.1:1.12: Shukla prints `idamucyate indriyā vaikalyaṁ` ('this is called the defectiveness of faculties') — but the definiendum at 1.9 is *indriyair avikalatā* (non-defectiveness), so the closing must read *indriyāṇām avaikalyam* (or *indriyāvaikalyam*) to match. Treated as a scribal/print error: the leading *a-* of *avaikalyam* has been lost, leaving *vaikalyam* in apparent contradiction with the opening. English silently corrects.
sbh1.1:1.13: *Prasāda* — rendered 'clarity' to keep it distinct from *śraddhā* 'faith,' which appears alongside it in 1.14 and 1.17. The source distinguishes the two: *śraddhā* is the active faith one gains, *prasāda* is the resulting serene-clarity-of-mind state; 1.17 says faith is the 'predominant forerunner' that produces *prasāda*. The standard Buddhist Studies rendering of *prasāda* is 'serene faith' / 'serene confidence' / 'lucid confidence,' which captures the faith-component bare 'clarity' loses; 'clarity' is kept here on consistency grounds and because *śraddhā* already carries the faith-rendering, but the connotation should be heard as faith-induced lucidity, not bare cognitive transparency. *Āyatana-gata* — 'gone-to/lodged-in [its proper] *āyatana*'; here the *āyatana* is the dharma-vinaya as object-locus of faith-clarity (1.16), distinct from the geographical *ārya-āyatana* at 1.7. Rendered 'directed to its sphere' with 'sphere' chosen over 'locus' to make the doctrinal-domain sense audible.
sbh1.1:1.18: *aparivṛttakarmāntatā* literally 'the state in which the karma-end has not been turned-around/sealed.' The five *ānantarya* (immediate-retribution) actions, once committed, are held to render the noble path unattainable in this very life — the karmic outcome is fixed. The contrast term in 1.21 (*parivṛttakarmāntatā*) is rendered 'obstructed action' for the same reason.
sbh1.1:1.22: *ātmabhāva* ('individual existence' / 'this present body-and-mind') and *ātmasampat* ('endowment-from-self') are distinct in the source. The first names what is brought to fulfillment; the second names the resulting category — the eight factors that arise within one's own continuum, contrasted with *parasampat* (endowment-from-others) in 1.24.
sbh1.1:1.26: *parataḥ pratyanukampā* — literally 'sympathy-in-response from another.' Rendered 'responsive support of others' to capture that this is concrete material support (food, robes, lodging, medicine) given in response to a renunciant's situation, not abstract benevolence.
sbh1.1:3.5: *Kalatra-varga* (visible in the extracted source as split/garbled `kaḍa la travarga`) is the spouse-and-family or household-circle being abandoned at going-forth; it is paired with wealth, grain, and gold, not another word for treasure.
sbh1.1:4.2: The going-forth definition is textually unstable around *upasampat-kuśalair aśīḥśīla-samādānaṁ vā*. The first half clearly refers to ordination through the formal *jñapti-caturtha* verbal act; the second half is taken functionally as undertaking training precepts from those skilled in full ordination. The English is marked conjectural/corrupt rather than treating the extracted phrase as secure.
sbh1.1:10.12: *Samudānayati* here is read as bringing forth/fulfilling the graded conditions for lineage-emergence, beginning with endowment-from-self and ending in dependence on concentration. The prior wording made the concentrations themselves seem to be the only referent.
sbh1.1:12.1: The second mark of the non-lineage person at 12.1–12.3 is governed by negation. Even after hearing about saṁsāra and nirvāṇa, he has not generated even slight fault-seeing or urgency regarding saṁsāra across the three times; regarding nirvāṇa, craving-destruction, dispassion, and cessation, only a limited and slight seeing of qualities/benefits and clarity arises. The previous English made him sound as if he did produce slight fault-seeing of saṁsāra, weakening the contrast.
sbh1.1:11.12: *sarvabuddhaiḥ āśrayasanniviṣṭā aprahāṇadharmiṇī* — read as 'lodged in the basis [such that, even by] all the Buddhas [it is] of the nature of non-abandonment.' Translation makes the implied counterfactual explicit ('even all the Buddhas could not uproot it'). The conventional reading takes *sarvabuddhaiḥ* as the agent against whose collective power the craving still resists.
sbh1.1:12.10: Source paragraph 12 of the original *sbh1* file collapsed the long fault-list into a single segment, leaving 12.11 with only a fragment. The two segments are restored here at the source's *|* boundary: 12.10 names the setup (the teaching's completeness for him), 12.11 carries the rest of the description and the negation.
sbh1.1:12.14: *Rājābhinirṇīta* / *caurābhinirṇīta* are motivational-pressure items in the stock list of bad reasons for going forth. 'Under pressure from a king/thieves' is intentionally broad; the point is coerced or fear-driven ordination, not being 'resolved upon' in the mental-act sense.
sbh1.1:14.4: *Niṣkrānta* is rendered 'gone out' in this path-taxonomy context to avoid confusing it with monastic going-forth (*pravrajita/pravrajyā*). The distinction is defined at 17.1–18.2: the descended-but-not-yet-gone-out person has not yet gained the noble path and its fruit; the descended-and-gone-out person has.
sbh1.1:19.2: The Shukla source reads *yasya nātyarthaṁ ... atyarthaṁ dhandhavāhīni indriyāṇi* — but the leading *nātyarthaṁ* is almost certainly scribal duplication from the next entry (*madhyendriya* in 20.2, which legitimately uses *nātyarthaṁ*). Read here without the *na*. The contrast across 19–21 then runs: mild = extremely sluggish, middle = not extremely sluggish, sharp = not sluggish at all (*a-dhandha-vāhīni*).
sbh1.1:21.7: *tanu vā* — literally 'or subtle.' Taken with the preceding clause (*arthasya āśu prativedhāya* — 'for swift penetration of meaning'), the modifier qualifies the meaning being penetrated: even subtle meaning yields to a sharp-faculty practitioner.
sbh1.1:26.1: The gotrabhūmi ends mid-list. The categories enumerated at 14.4–14.7 ('matured / not matured', 'purified / not purified', 'far / near') are not all given their own definition blocks here: 'far' is defined at 25, but 'matured', 'purified', and 'near' transition directly into the avatārabhūmi. In the source, *āsanne pudgalaḥ* is followed immediately by *II. avatārabhūmiḥ — yaiḥ ṣaḍbhir bhavyo…*, so the next file ([sbh1.2](sbh1.2.html#sbh1.2:1.1)) effectively serves as the answer to 'what is the near person?' (becoming near to nirvāṇa is what the descent-stage describes).
